_doc: The countries of the Central Bank (CB) page: DM (US, Euro Area plus DE, FR, IT, ES, UK, Japan, Switzerland, Canada, Australia, Sweden, Norway, New Zealand, South Korea) and the BRICS EM (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa and the newer members Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE, Indonesia). South Korea, Australia, Canada and Indonesia are named explicitly and appear once. Codes: id is the page key (ISO 3166 alpha-2, EA the euro area); iso3 the IMF DataMapper code (EURO is not an IMF weight series: the euro area weight is the sum of weight_members); wb the World Bank code; bis the BIS code (XM euro area); oecd the OECD Economic Outlook area (null: not covered). aggregate=false marks a member already counted inside the Euro Area, so the DM and World aggregates never count it twice. inflation_target is the bank's published target (null: none declared, the model row then answers n/a). The World aggregate covers the economies listed here, not the whole world.

options.label: PPP

options.label: Market FX
options.source: IMF WEO DataMapper, GDP at current prices (US dollars)

weights._doc: The aggregate of a group is the GDP-weighted mean of the countries with a value: weights are the IMF GDP of the same year, re-normalised over the countries that have a number; a country with n/a drops out of both sums. Toggle in the page.

ui.note_countries: Aggregates are GDP-weighted means of the countries that have a value (weights re-normalised); heat compares a value with the country's own history. — = n/a (no free source).
ui.note_groups: World covers the economies listed here, not the whole world; the euro-area members DE, FR, IT and ES are inside the Euro Area.
ui.note_predictions: Forecasts: IMF WEO and OECD Economic Outlook for the current year, +1 and +2. Taylor path: the model's implied policy rate from the forecast inflation, the OECD output gap and the potential growth as the neutral rate; a model, not a bank forecast.

taylor._doc: Taylor-rule implied policy rate = neutral + inflation + inflation_weight x (inflation - target) + gap_weight x output gap, where neutral is the OECD potential growth, inflation is the headline forecast of the year, target is the bank's declared inflation_target and gap the OECD output gap. Missing any input: n/a. Bias = implied minus the latest policy rate: above +hold_band_pp tightening, below -hold_band_pp easing, else hold.

years._doc: history = years of actuals kept before the current year; forecast = current year, +1, +2
